# Results — Study 135 (FOMC-Cycle) on real SPY daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One claim — US equity returns since
1994 accrue in the **even weeks** (0, 2, 4) of the ~6-week FOMC cycle and are flat in odd weeks
(1, 3, 5) — tested on SPY daily total returns with FOMC meeting dates from the Federal Reserve's
published schedule. Cieslak, Morse & Vuolteenaho (2019, "Stock Returns over the FOMC Cycle",
Journal of Finance). As-of **2026-06-14**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|
| SPY daily (Yahoo, `last_call_spy.parquet`) | 1994-01-03 → 2026-06-11 | `b679e9c9c5a2` |
| FOMC schedule | 1994-02-04 → 2026-06-17 | hardcoded (Fed calendars) |

n = **8,141** trading days with a valid cycle-week label (24 days before the first FOMC in 1994
have NaN). Of these, **3,881** fall in even weeks (0, 2, 4) and **4,260** in odd weeks (1, 3, 5).

## The headline test — even weeks vs odd weeks

| Arm | n | mean (bps/day) | HAC t | ann. Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Even weeks (0, 2, 4)** | 3,881 | **+6.58** | **+3.94** | **+0.90** |
| Odd weeks (1, 3, 5) | 4,260 | +3.07 | +1.74 | +0.40 |
| All days (buy-and-hold) | 8,141 | +4.75 | +4.20 | +0.64 |

- Even-week mean is elevated and individually significant (HAC *t* = **+3.94**).
- But the *gap* (even − odd) is only **+3.51 bps/day** with a Welch *t* = **+1.34** —
  not statistically significant at the 5% level.
- The buy-and-hold baseline (all days) has *t* = 4.20 and Sharpe 0.64 — close to the
  even-week arm, suggesting most of the premium is simply equity risk premium rather than
  a FOMC-cycle anomaly.

## Week-by-week breakdown

| Cycle week | n | mean (bps/day) | HAC t | Even? |
|---|--:|--:|--:|:---:|
| **0** | 1,315 | **+6.53** | **+2.14** | Yes |
| 1 | 1,315 | +3.19 | +1.03 | — |
| **2** | 1,307 | **+5.76** | **+1.96** | Yes |
| 3 | 1,297 | +5.15 | +1.65 | — |
| **4** | 1,259 | **+7.49** | **+2.88** | Yes |
| 5 | 1,648 | +1.34 | +0.48 | — |

Week 4 is the strongest individual week (t = 2.88); week 5 is the weakest (t = 0.48).
The week-3 mean (+5.15 bps) is nearly as high as even weeks, which complicates the
even-vs-odd framing.

## Post-publication decay (McLean & Pontiff 2016)

The paper was published in 2019 (Journal of Finance, 74:5). Splitting the sample:

| Era | Even-minus-odd gap | Welch t | n (even/odd) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Pre-2019 (in-sample for paper) | **+5.07 bps/day** | **+1.71** | 2,986 / 3,284 |
| Post-2019 (out-of-sample) | **−1.72 bps/day** | **−0.30** | 895 / 976 |

The gap is **gone post-publication** — in fact it reversed sign. This is consistent with
the McLean-Pontiff (2016) finding that anomaly returns shrink after documentation.

## Placebo test (random cycle-week permutation)

Shuffling the even/odd labels 500 times: the real gap (+3.51 bps) exceeds the placebo
distribution at the **p = 0.112** level. The null is not rejected at 5% — the gap could
plausibly be noise under i.i.d. labels.

- Placebo mean: +0.04 bps/day, std: 2.75 bps.
- Real gap at 88th percentile of the placebo distribution.

## Could you trade it? — cost and turnover

The "long even weeks, flat odd weeks" strategy enters and exits ~48 times per year
(3 even-week blocks × 8 meetings × 2 transitions). Costs are modest by daily standards:

| Round-trip cost | Gross ann. | Net ann. |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0.0 bps | +16.6%/yr | +16.6%/yr |
| 0.5 bps | +16.6%/yr | +16.3%/yr |
| 1.0 bps | +16.6%/yr | +16.1%/yr |
| 2.0 bps | +16.6%/yr | +15.6%/yr |
| 5.0 bps | +16.6%/yr | +14.2%/yr |

However, the gross return is almost entirely explained by equity risk (buy-and-hold SPY
earns +16.6%/yr on even-week days alone, simply because they represent 48% of all
trading days). The incremental return vs buy-and-hold is the only honest performance
measure, and the Welch-t on that gap is 1.34 — not statistically distinguishable from
zero. Post-2019, the premium is negative, so a live implementation since publication
would have underperformed a simple buy-and-hold.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery works

On a deterministic synthetic tape (`data.synthetic_cycle`) with a planted even-week
premium of +10 bps/day, the engine correctly identifies the gap (Welch-t ≈ 2.7) and
produces no false positives on the null tape (premium = 0, Welch-t ≈ 0.72).

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** Even weeks show elevated returns historically (HAC *t* = 3.94),
  but the direct even-vs-odd Welch *t* = 1.34 falls short of the inference bar. The gap
  is consistent with the CMV (2019) finding for the pre-publication era (+5.07 bps,
  t = 1.71) but has completely reversed post-2019 (−1.72 bps, t = −0.30). Placebo
  p = 0.112 also fails to reject the null. The literature support is real, but the
  out-of-sample evidence is absent.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The gross premium over buy-and-hold (Welch-t 1.34) is
  statistically insufficient to justify tactical timing even at near-zero cost. Post-2019
  the live strategy underperforms buy-and-hold by 1.72 bps/day (~4.3%/yr).
- **Post-publication decay — CONFIRMED.** Pre-2019: +5.07 bps, t = 1.71.
  Post-2019: −1.72 bps, t = −0.30. The edge, to the extent it ever existed, has decayed
  to zero and beyond after documentation.
